queue.name: Farigh-Brega Gas Pipeline
queue.note: 42in, ~130km (2006 CPECC contract was for 215km) line from Zueitina Field 103/103A (fed by Farigh field, also called Intisar A/103) via Km 91 complex into Sirte Oil's Line 36B / Brega network; halted pre-2011, phase-1 (30km) opened Mar 2026, full line trial-run Apr 2026. No roster row matches this route/history under any of its names. Closest is P1856 Intesar-Brega Gas Pipeline (also 42in, same general Intisar/Zueitina-to-Brega corridor) but P1856's length (333km) is more than 2x this project's built length and P1856 is already status=operating, whereas every 2026 source describes this line as only now emerging from a 16-year construction halt -- vetter should confirm whether this is a genuinely separate/parallel segment (own PID) or whether P1856 needs a length/status correction instead of a new row.
aka: Zueitina Field 103-Sirte Oil Line 36B Gas Pipeline
Intisar A/103 to Brega Gas Pipeline
Gas Transfer Project 103 Intisar Field to a Coastal Network
Intisar A/103 to Brega Gas Distribution Network
queue.sponsor: National Oil Corporation (NOC), via Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Company and Zueitina Oil Company (Waha Oil Company system); original 2006 contractor CPECC
queue.from: Farigh field / Zueitina Oil Company Field 103-103A supply base (Sirte Basin) -- also described as the Intisar A/103 field
queue.to: Km 91 complex, tying into Sirte Oil Company's 42-inch Line 36B / Brega coastal gas network
queue.status_guess: construction (phase 1 operating since Mar 2026; full 130km line in trial operation as of Apr 2026)

evidence.note: NOC inaugurates first phase (30km) linking Farigh field/Field 103A to the 42in Sirte trunkline at km 91, feeding Brega by end of month.
First phase (~30km) linking Field 103/Farigh system into existing 42in pipeline supplying Brega and the coastal network.
Libya Observer's own report, naming the project the 'Farigh-Brega Gas Pipeline'.
Independent corroboration of March first-phase launch, same specs (30km, Zueitina axis Field 103A to km-91 trunkline).
NOC Chairman hails completion of the full 42in, 130km pipeline from Zueitina Field 103 to Sirte Oil Line 36B at km 91; halted pre-2011, now finished; ~150 mmcf/d capacity.
Trial operation of the 42in, 130km line connecting Intisar A/103 field to the Brega network; stalled ~16 years; recovers ~150 mmcf/d flared gas.
Full-line test (Apr 13, 2026) of the 42in ~130km Intisar A/103-Brega line; recovers ~150 mmcf/d previously flared; stalled 16+ years.
In-brief on the same April trial-operation milestone, calling it a 'strategic gas pipeline'.
Trial run of the 42in ~130km line linking Intisar A/103 to Brega; recovers flared gas from Intisar, Irada and Sahel fields; stalled 16+ years.
First 30km phase of the Farigh-Brega pipeline commissioned and flowing; references a 2 Bcf/d full-capacity target by 2030, implying further phases.
'Al-Intisar to Brega' 42in pipeline entered experimental operation Apr 23, 2026 after connection works completed.
Independent report of the same 130km/42in Intisar A/103-Brega trial run, April 14, 2026.

Original 2006 construction history: Zueitina Oil Co. letter of intent to CPECC for a 215km, 42in, 1,500mmcf/d pipeline from Zueitina's 103A supply base to the Brega coastal pipeline, gas sourced from the Faregh field and Zueitina concession.
